moral_character_required.quote: Every person desiring to practice optometry in this state shall be 19 years of age, or over, a citizen of the United States or, if not a citizen of the United States, a person who is legally present in the United States with appropriate documentation from the federal government, and of good moral character.

interval_years.quote: the licensee shall receive the current annual registration certificate authorizing him or her to continue the practice of optometry in this state for a period of one year.

renewal_fee_usd.quote: Every licensed optometrist who desires to continue the practice of optometry in the state shall annually, on or before the first day of October, pay to the secretary of the board a renewal fee of one hundred sixty dollars ($160)

required.quote: All registered optometrists licensed in the State of Alabama are required to take annual courses of study in subjects relating to the practice of optometry.

hours_per_period.quote: The length of study shall be prescribed by the board but shall not exceed 25 clock hours in any calendar year.

period_years.quote: All registered optometrists licensed in the State of Alabama are required to take annual courses of study in subjects relating to the practice of optometry.

value: diagnosis, treatment, and management of disease of the human eye and its adjacent structures (for pharmaceutical agent licensees, at least half of required hours)
topical_requirements.quote: Licensees approved by the board to use pharmaceutical agents shall be required to take not less than 20 nor more than 25 hours of continuing education, half of which shall be in subjects relating to the diagnosis, treatment, and management of disease of the human eye and its adjacent structures.

available.quote: Any person who has successfully passed a standard examination in optometry in any state of the United States or all parts of the examination given by the National Board of Examiners in Optometry and is the holder of a certificate to that effect, issued by the board of that state, or by the national board, and who has a current license to practice optometry in any state in the United States, and has conducted an ethical professional practice of optometry for at least one year, may, at the discretion of the board, and upon the payment of the amount of the regular examination fee, take the standard examination, and upon passing the examination be registered as qualified to practice optometry in this state.

requirements.value: Applicant must have passed a standard examination in optometry in another state or all parts of the NBEO exam, hold a current license in any U.S. state, and have conducted an ethical professional practice for at least one year. At board discretion, applicant pays the regular examination fee and must pass the Alabama standard examination.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Fraud, deceit, dishonesty, or misrepresentation in the practice of optometry or in obtaining any license or certificate.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Fraud, deceit, dishonesty, or misrepresentation, whether knowingly or unknowingly, in the practice of optometry or in obtaining any license, license certificate, annual registration certificate, or other thing of value.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Conviction of a felony or a misdemeanor involving moral turpitude.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Conviction of a felony or a misdemeanor which involves moral turpitude.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Habitual drunkenness or addiction to morphine, cocaine, or similar drugs.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Habitual drunkenness or addiction to the use of morphine, cocaine, or other drugs having similar effect.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Insanity as adjudged by a court of competent jurisdiction.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Insanity, as adjudged by a court of competent jurisdiction.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Directly or indirectly employing or inducing an unlicensed person to practice optometry.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Directly or indirectly employing, hiring, procuring, or inducing a person, not licensed to practice optometry in this state, to so practice.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Aiding or abetting the practice of optometry by an unlicensed person.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Directly or indirectly aiding or abetting in the practice of optometry any person not duly licensed to practice under this chapter.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Employing solicitors, canvassers, or agents to obtain patronage.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Directly or indirectly employing solicitors, canvassers, or agents for the purpose of obtaining patronage.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Willfully or repeatedly violating any provision of the chapter.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Willfully or repeatedly violating any of the provisions of this chapter.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Practicing optometry under a name other than one's own as set forth on the license certificate.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Practicing or attempting to practice optometry under a name other than one's own name as set forth on the license certificate.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Lending, leasing, or placing one's license at the disposal of an unlicensed person.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Lending, leasing, renting, or in any other manner placing his or her license or license certificate at the disposal or in the service of any person not licensed to practice optometry in this state.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Soliciting patients by fraudulent or misleading advertising.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Soliciting patients by fraudulent or misleading advertising of any kind, nature, or description.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failing to comply with the continuing education requirements established by the board.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failing to comply with the continuing education requirements established by the board pursuant to the provisions of this chapter.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Practicing optometry in a temporary office apart from a regularly established office, unless meeting branch office requirements.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Practicing optometry in any temporary office, apart from a regularly established office; provided, that a licensed optometrist may establish a branch office if the branch office is duly equipped with the instruments necessary, according to rules and regulations promulgated by the board, to make complete optometric examination

disciplinary_grounds.description: Practicing optometry as an employee on a fee-splitting basis.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Practicing optometry as the employee of any person, group, association, or corporation on the basis of any fee splitting or on any basis which has the effect of any such agreement

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violating any other standards of professional conduct adopted by the board as rules.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Violating any other standards of professional conduct as may be adopted as rules by the board.

definition_quote.value: The practice of optometry is a learned profession involving the examination, measurement by objective and subjective means, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of any departure from the normal of the human eyes, their adjacent structures, and visual system.
definition_quote.quote: The practice of optometry is a learned profession involving the examination, measurement by objective and subjective means, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of any departure from the normal of the human eyes, their adjacent structures, and visual system.

value: adapting and fitting all types of lenses or devices including contact lenses
determination of refractive error and visual/muscular/anatomical anomalies
determination and prescribing of spectacle or contact lens parameters
administering and prescribing pharmaceutical agents for diagnosis and treatment of eye diseases
removal of superficial foreign bodies from the human eye and adjacent structures
providing developmental and perceptual therapy for the vision system
utilization of any method or means to diagnose and treat diseases of the human eye
performance of primary eye care procedures or ordering of laboratory tests
prescribing and administering narcotic analgesics (except Schedule I, II, and III Hydrocodone)
prescribing and administering steroids
administering epinephrine, benadryl, or other medication to counteract anaphylaxis
methods_authorized.quote: The practice of optometry includes but is not limited to: The adapting and fitting of all types of lenses or devices, including, contact lenses; the determination of refractive error and shape of the eye and visual, muscular, or anatomical anomalies of the eye through the use of any means including the use of any self testing devices and the use of any computerized or automatic refracting device; the determination and prescribing of spectacle or contact lens parameters; the administering and prescription of pharmaceutical agents rational to the diagnosis and treatment of disease of the human eye and its adjacent structures; the removal of superficial foreign bodies from the human eye and its adjacent structures; the providing of developmental and perceptual therapy for the vision system

drug_authority.value: Optometrists approved by the board may prescribe and administer pharmaceutical agents for treatment of the human eye and adjacent structures, including narcotic analgesics except Schedule I and II and Schedule III agents containing Hydrocodone; other Schedule III agents limited to 96-hour prescriptions; steroids; and anaphylaxis medications.
drug_authority.quote: The practice of optometry shall include the prescribing and administering of narcotic analgesics pursuant to the Alabama Uniform Controlled Substances Act, except for narcotic analgesics classified under Schedule I and II, and any Schedule III pharmaceutical agents that contain Dihydrocodeinone, ("Hydrocodone"). The prescribing or administering of any other Schedule III pharmaceutical agent shall be limited to a prescription, the duration of which does not exceed 96 hours.

surgery_prohibited.quote: Optometrists are prohibited from performing injections into the eyeball, cataract surgery, muscle surgery, retinal surgery, radial keratotomy, laser surgery, cryosurgery, or any other invasive surgery.

surgery_definition.value: Invasive surgery including injections into the eyeball, cataract surgery, muscle surgery, retinal surgery, radial keratotomy, laser surgery, and cryosurgery.
surgery_definition.quote: Optometrists are prohibited from performing injections into the eyeball, cataract surgery, muscle surgery, retinal surgery, radial keratotomy, laser surgery, cryosurgery, or any other invasive surgery.

foreign_body_removal_authorized.quote: the removal of superficial foreign bodies from the human eye and its adjacent structures

anaphylaxis_treatment_authorized.quote: The practice of optometry shall include the authority to administer benedryl, epinephrine, or other medication to counteract anaphylaxis or anaphylactic reaction.

vision_therapy_authorized.quote: the providing of developmental and perceptual therapy for the vision system

pharmaceutical_certification_required.quote: The use and prescribing of pharmaceutical agents for the treatment of the human eye and its adjacent structures shall be limited to those optometrists approved by the board.

specialty_certification_types.quote: A seal of approval by the board of the use of pharmaceutical agents for the treatment of the human eye and any of its adjacent structures shall be affixed to the license certificate.

pharmacology_training_hours_required.quote: the requirement that the applicant has successfully completed at least 72 clock hours in the diagnosis and management of disease of the human eye and its adjacent structures within a three-year period preceding application for a license.

delegation_to_unlicensed_assistants_auth.quote: A provider may delegate tasks and activities at an established treatment site to an assistant who is properly trained and supervised or directed.

telemedicine_authorized.quote: TELEMEDICINE. A health service that is delivered by a licensed optometrist acting within the scope of his or her license and that requires the use of advanced telecommunications technology

home_visit_permit_required.quote: A patient's private home is not considered an established treatment site.

impaired_practitioner_program_establishe.quote: IMPAIRED DOCTOR OF OPTOMETRY TREATMENT PROGRAM. The Alabama Board of Optometry approved or sponsored program for the detection, intervention, and monitoring of impaired providers.

limited_teaching_license_available.quote: The board may, under rules and regulations to be promulgated by the board, issue limited licenses, in the case of teachers, to persons who hold an optometric degree where such persons are not licensed and registered to practice optometry in this state.

retired_license_status_available.quote: The board may waive annual registration and the payment of fees while any licensee is prevented from practicing optometry by reason of physical disability, temporary active duty with any of the Armed Forces of the United States, or while any licensee is completely retired from the practice of optometry.
